title: myCHEF vs Taste Studio: comparing event service scope
body_html:
Choosing between myCHEF and Taste Studio in 2026 comes down to service scope: myCHEF puts a vetted chef in your kitchen or caters your event, while Taste Studio should be judged on its own published menus and service format. Choose myCHEF if you want a chef who cooks for you and your guests; choose Taste Studio if its menu and format already fit an event you have scoped.

TL;DR
  • myCHEF suits hosts who want a vetted private chef, weekly meal prep or a fully designed event in Dubai.
  • Taste Studio suits buyers whose event matches its published menus and service format, once confirmed in writing.
  • For a mychef vs taste studio service comparison in 2026, compare scope, staffing and dietary handling, not headline style.
  • Ask both for a written scope before paying a deposit.

Why this comparison matters in 2026

Two Dubai food suppliers can both be called "catering" and still deliver very different things. One sends a chef to cook in your home. Another prepares food elsewhere and delivers it. A third manages staff, equipment and service on the night.

The label tells you little. The scope tells you everything. This page compares what myCHEF offers against the questions you should put to Taste Studio, so you can decide on scope rather than on a website's tone.

Evidence note: the myCHEF details below come from myCHEF's own service description. Taste Studio details are not asserted here. Confirm them directly with Taste Studio before you book.

At a glance

Dimension myCHEF Taste Studio
Best for Home-cooked meals, weekly meal prep, dinner parties, corporate events, large celebrations Events that match its published menus and format; confirm directly
Service model Vetted chefs, menus designed around the client Confirm whether chefs cook on site or food is prepared off site
Household services Private chef and weekly meal prep Ask whether recurring household cooking is offered
Event services Dinner parties, corporate events, large catered celebrations Ask for event types, guest-count range and staffing
Standards Halal-first, chefs vetted and scored Request halal status and sourcing in writing
Pricing model Quoted around the brief; live household rates on the pricing page Request an itemised quote
Kitchen cleanup Kitchen left exactly as found Ask what is included

myCHEF offers a wider range of in-home services

myCHEF covers four things under one roof: home-cooked meals, weekly meal prep, dinner parties and larger catered celebrations. A household can start with a single dinner and move to a recurring arrangement without changing supplier.

That matters if your needs change. A family that books one birthday dinner often asks about weekly meals a month later.

  • Home-cooked meals: a chef cooks in your kitchen, to your menu.
  • Weekly meal prep: recurring cooking for a household routine.
  • Dinner parties: a designed menu for a set guest count.
  • Corporate and large events: catering for businesses and celebrations.

If you only need a single drop-off order, this breadth is unnecessary. If you want one team that handles a dinner, a weekly routine and a company event, it is a real advantage.

Taste Studio is the one to check on format

The honest position: Taste Studio may be the better fit if you want food delivered to a venue and have no need for a chef in your home. Many events need exactly that, and a chef in the kitchen adds cost and logistics you may not want.

What decides it is whether Taste Studio's format matches your event. Ask three questions:

  1. Is the food cooked on site, or prepared elsewhere and delivered?
  2. Are service staff, equipment and setup included, or quoted separately?
  3. What is the guest-count range it handles comfortably?

Until those are answered in writing, you are comparing a website with a scope. They are not the same.

Chef vetting: myCHEF states its process

myCHEF describes its chefs as vetted and scored before they cook for a client. For a private booking, where a stranger works in your kitchen, that is the most important line on the page.

When comparing suppliers, ask how chefs are checked, who is sent to your event and whether you can see a menu before the date. A supplier that answers precisely is easier to trust than one that answers warmly.

This dimension is a draw until Taste Studio's process is confirmed. A stated process from myCHEF beats no answer, but it does not beat a good answer.

Halal and dietary handling

myCHEF works halal-first. For many Dubai hosts this is a baseline, not a preference, and it should be explicit for any supplier you consider.

For allergies, vegan or gluten-free guests, send the list with your first enquiry. Do not leave it for the week of the event. Ask each supplier how cross-contact is handled and whether a separate dish or a separate preparation area is offered.

For broader options, the guides on halal catering companies in Dubai and gluten-free catering list what to ask.

Menu design: built around you vs choose from a list

myCHEF designs menus around the client. You give a guest count, a date, dietary needs and a style; the menu follows. That suits hosts who know the feeling they want but not the dishes.

A set-menu supplier suits hosts who want to choose quickly and compare line by line. Both approaches are valid. The mistake is assuming one supplier offers both.

Verdict: myCHEF wins for bespoke menus; a set-menu supplier wins on speed of comparison. Taste Studio's approach should be confirmed on its own menu pages.

Cleanup and kitchen respect

When a chef works in your home, the kitchen is the real test. myCHEF leaves the kitchen exactly as it found it. That is a specific promise you can hold a supplier to.

If you book any on-site cooking service, ask the same question and get the answer in the quote. Cleanup is easy to promise and easy to forget on the night.

Start an enquiry

Pricing: compare the model, not the headline

No prices are quoted here, because rates change and a number on this page would go stale. What you can compare is the pricing model.

  • Quoted around a brief: price follows guest count, menu and service level. It flexes with your event, but you need a written quote to compare.
  • Fixed packages: easier to compare at a glance, less flexible when your brief is unusual.

Whichever you pick, ask for an itemised quote that separates food, staffing, equipment and travel. For household costs, read the guide on how much a private chef costs in Dubai and then check the live pricing before you decide.

Scorecard

Dimension Winner
Household range (chef plus meal prep) myCHEF
Bespoke menu design myCHEF
Stated chef vetting myCHEF, pending Taste Studio's answer
Halal-first standard myCHEF stated; confirm Taste Studio
Simple delivered food for a venue Taste Studio, if its format fits
Price transparency Tie until both provide itemised quotes

Final verdict

Choose myCHEF if:

  • You want a chef cooking in your home or at your own venue.
  • You need recurring meal prep as well as one-off events.
  • Halal-first standards and a vetted chef matter to you.

Choose Taste Studio if:

  • Its published menus and service format match an event you have already scoped.
  • You want food delivered rather than cooked in your kitchen.
  • Its written quote is itemised and clearer than the alternative.

The quotable version: myCHEF is the stronger choice in 2026 for hosts who want a vetted private chef and a menu designed around them; Taste Studio is worth a quote if you only need catering that matches its format.

FAQ

Is myCHEF better than Taste Studio?

It depends on scope. myCHEF is better for in-home private chef work and weekly meal prep. Taste Studio should be judged on its own menus and format, which you should confirm in writing.

Does myCHEF cook in my home?

Yes. myCHEF provides vetted chefs for home-cooked meals, dinner parties and weekly meal prep, and leaves the kitchen exactly as found.

Is myCHEF halal?

myCHEF works halal-first. Send any further dietary requirements with your enquiry so the menu is designed around them.

Can myCHEF cater corporate events?

Yes. myCHEF caters corporate events and large celebrations as well as private dinners. Share the date, location and guest count for a tailored quote.

What should I ask Taste Studio before booking?

Ask whether food is cooked on site, what staffing and equipment are included, and for an itemised written quote. Also confirm halal status and allergy handling.

How do I compare two catering quotes fairly?

Ask both for the same brief: date, guest count, dietary needs and service level. Compare food, staffing, equipment and travel as separate lines.

One last thing

The cheapest way to compare is to send the same three-line brief to both suppliers on the same day. The one that asks better questions back has usually thought harder about your event.
